newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WELLS STRIKES OUT 16, MARTINEZ BELTS 36TH FOR YANKEES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WELLS STRIKES OUT 16, MARTINEZ BELTS 36TH FOR YANKEES.

text.p: Tino Martinez blasted his major league-leading 36th home run and David Wells struck out 16 in a masterful three-hitter to lead the New York Yankees to a 7-0 victory over the Oakland Athletics on Wednesday.
Wells (11-5) allowed just three singles and his 16 strikeouts tied for the second-best in franchise history, two shy of the mark Ron Guidry set in 1978.

Martinez belted a two-run homer in the first inning to stake the Yankees to a 3-0 lead. The 36 home runs are the most by a Yankees first baseman since Lou Gehrig hit 37 in 1937. Martinez also leads the majors with 99 RBI.
"I'm just trying to play every day and I'll look at my numbers at the end of the year," Martinez said.
Luis Sojo went 4-for-5 with a home run and two RBI for the Yankees, who completed a sweep of the three-game series.
It was the second shutout for Wells in his last three starts and his fourth complete game of the season.

"You get ahead in the count and don't make a mistake, you can bury them," said Wells, who did not allow a hit until Scott Spiezio singled off the glove of third baseman Wage Boggs with one out in the fifth inning.
Izzy Molina had the only other hits for Oakland -- a two-out single in the fifth inning and a single in the eighth.
Oakland's Steve Karsay (3-11) lasted just three innings, allowing six runs and eight hits.
The loss was the fifth in a row and 10th in 12 games for the Athletics, who have scored three runs or less in nine of their last 10 contests.
In Boston, Nomar Garciaparra drilled a bases-loaded single with two out in the bottom of the 10th inning to lift the Red Sox to an 8-7 victory over the Seattle Mariners.
With two out in the 10th, Edwin Hurtado (1-2) allowed a single to Jesus Tavarez before walking Darren Bragg and Jeff Frye on eight pitches to load the bases.
Garciaparra followed by pulling a 1-1 pitch off the "Green Monster" left-field wall to end the game as the Red Sox erased a late five-run deficit to post their fourth straight victory.
Bragg had a pair of RBI doubles and Frye also drove in runs in the eighth and ninth as the Seattle bullpen blew a 7-2 lead over the two innings.
Edgar Martinez had a three-run homer for Seattle.

In Chicago, Frank Thomas snapped a tie with a sixth-inning homer and Doug Drabek and four relievers combined on a six-hitter as the White Sox snapped a four-game losing streak with a 3-2 victory over the Detroit Tigers.

Tigers starter Scott Sanders (3-8) had retired 12 consecutive batters when Thomas belted his 25th homer with one out in the sixth. He hit a 1-0 pitch over the centre-field fence, giving Chicago a 3-2 lead.
Drabek (7-7) gave up two runs and five hits in six innings to snap a personal three-game losing streak.

In Baltimore, Scott Kamieniecki allowed one run over 6 2/3 innings and Geronimo Berroa had a two-run single in the fourth as the Orioles completed a three-game sweep of the Texas Rangers with a 3-1 victory.
Jeff Reboulet, filling in for the injured Roberto Alomar at second base, went 3-for-4 with an RBI for Baltimore, which extended its winning streak to five games.
Kamieniecki (7-5) allowed three hits and four walks while fanning six. He allowed no hits after a second-inning single by Warren Newson. Randy Myers earned his 30th save in 31 opportunities.

In Kansas City, Brad Radke easily won his team-record 11th consecutive start and Marty Cordova, Denny Hocking and Chuck Knoblauch each drove in two runs in an eight-run first inning as the Minnesota Twins crushed the Royals 11-1.
Radke (15-5) gave up one run and three hits with three walks and two strikeouts over seven innings. He didn't allow a hit until Chili Davis's two-out single in the sixth inning.
Minnesota sent 12 men to the plate in the first inning with nine straight reaching base at one point as Glendon Rusch (3-7) was torched for 10 runs and nine hits over three innings.
In Cleveland, Ken Hill pitched 6 1/3 innings to win his Anaheim debut and Jim Edmonds homered and drove in two runs as the Angels completed a four-game sweep of the Indians with a 5-2 victory.
Hill (6-8), acquired Tuesday from Texas, gave up five hits with seven walks and four strikeouts and Mike James retired all seven batters he faced to pick up the save.

Todd Greene led off the fifth against starter Charles Nagy (10-7) with a home run that snapped a 2-2 tie. The victory moved Anaheim within a half game of first-place Seattle in the American League West.
